title: How Israel’s elections could bring thaw with Syria
gist: Al-Monitor analysis argues a less hard-line Israeli government after the Oct. 27, 2026 election could open a thaw with Syria, driven by border stability, alignment with Washington and anti-Iran cooperation.

insights.claim: A less hard-line Israeli government after the Oct. 27, 2026 election would have incentives to stabilize its northern border with Syria, align with Washington's regional priorities and explore cooperation with Damascus against Iran.
insights.speaker: Ezgi Akin
insights.so_what: Election outcome is a swing factor for Israel-Syria de-escalation; watch coalition composition.

insights.claim: Netanyahu faces a tough challenge from ex-military chief Gadi Eisenkot, whose centrist Yashar party leads the opposition in several polls and who has teamed with a bloc including Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid on a joint ticket.
insights.speaker: Ezgi Akin
insights.so_what: Opposition is consolidated; polls are competitive, so a government change is plausible.

insights.claim: About 7.3 million Israelis are eligible to vote in the Oct. 27 election, which could reshape the political landscape of one of the Middle East's most powerful states.
insights.speaker: Ezgi Akin
insights.so_what: Sets the scale of a high-stakes regional event.

insights.claim: Netanyahu and his far-right coalition partners hold hard-line positions toward the post-Assad Damascus government; National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir last year called for assassinating President Ahmed al-Sharaa.
insights.speaker: Ezgi Akin
insights.so_what: A continued right-wing government implies persistent Israel-Syria hostility.
insights.locator: Netanyahu and his far-right coalition partners
